where: Worked example 1, steps 1–5 and answer (and quiz Q3 that depends on it)
problem: The machine M is called a machine that accepts strings ending in 1, but its accept state q1 also has outgoing transitions (q1,1 → q1,R and q1,0 → q0,R). Under the standard textbook convention a Turing machine halts the moment it enters the accept state, so M halts after only 1 move on 101, and the same machine would also accept 10, 100 and every other string starting with 1 — it does not accept exactly the strings ending in 1. The run of 3 moves is only valid under the other convention (a state may be final and still move; M accepts if it halts in q1), and the chapter never says which convention it uses.
fix: State the convention explicitly before the example, e.g. 'M has no reject state: it halts when no rule applies, and it accepts when it halts in q1 (a final state may still have moves).' Then the 3-move run and the answer are correct under that convention. If the standard halting-accept convention is kept, redesign M, for example: q0 (start), q1 (last symbol read was 1), q2 (accept); rules q0,0 → q0,R; q0,1 → q1,R; q1,0 → q0,R; q1,1 → q1,R; q1,blank → q2,R; no rule for q0 on blank, so it halts and rejects. On 101 this gives: move 1 q0,1 → q1 (head cell 1); move 2 q1,0 → q0 (head cell 2); move 3 q0,1 → q1 (head cell 3, blank); move 4 q1,blank → q2 accept. Then the answer and quiz Q3 become 4 simulated moves with final state q2.
